links.outcome: Reading ease and grade level of original versus AI-generated plain-language radiology reports
links.effect: Original reports were at college level (FKRL 12.2-15.4); AI reports improved FRES (e.g., MRI 20.3 to 66.9) but FKRL remained about 8.4-8.5, still above a typical 6th-grade target.
links.quote: There was also a statistically significant improvement in mean FKRL scores in the AI-LLM generated X-Ray report (12.2 ± 1.1 to 8.5 ± 0.4), CT report (15.4 ± 2.0 to 8.4 ± 0.6) and MRI report (14.1 ± 1.6 to 8.5 ± 0.5), all p < 0.001.

links.outcome: Hallucination rate in AI-generated patient-facing radiology explanations
links.effect: Hallucination rates were 4% (X-ray), 7% (CT), and 6% (MRI); mean Likert accuracy scores were 4.0, 3.9, and 3.9 out of 5.
links.quote: The rate of hallucinations in the AI-LLM generated X-Ray report, CT report and MRI report was 4%, 7% and 6%, respectively.

unlisted_practices: Using LLM prompting to translate radiology reports into layman's terms to improve readability

screen.reason: The study evaluates an LLM's baseline capability to simplify foot and ankle radiology reports for patients (measuring readability, accuracy, and hallucination rates), but it does not compare outcomes with and without a specific deployment safeguard or operational practice.
